prerequisites: It is recommended not to take this subject until a comprehensive vision of the technical disciplines taught in the degree has been achieved.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the legal and ethical requirements and implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle, and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social, and ethical conditions to be considered in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all necessary tasks to carry it out, and monitor progress and supervise the work to be performed in a project, keeping in mind the initial planning.
Clearly explain and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Know the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as develop and improve a work method.

syllabus_topics: Topic 4 Project Life Cycle. Preliminary Studies
Topic 5 Project Life Cycle. Engineering and Execution
Topic 7: Regulatory Framework and Project Processing.
Topic 8: Graphic Documentation of the Project
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (problem solving and case studies)
Computer lab practices (planning and budgeting techniques, graphic tools, document management)
assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in each of the three evaluated parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 * EV-1 + 0.35 * EV-2 + 0.25 * EV-3. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For EV-2, the average of two individual assignments must be above 4.0; if not, the average is capped at 4.0. For EV-3, the grade is 0.5 * (exercises done in class) + 0.5 * (lab practice exam). In the extraordinary call, grades above 5 from the ordinary call can be saved for individual components; if taken again, the new grade applies.
